title: Boss: the flash sale outage
summary: Explain an outage with numbers, take work off the synchronous path, size the consumers and give a new service a replayable history.

steps.title: INC-4107: checkout times out during the flash sale
body: **INC-4107 (SEV-2)** · opened 12:06 by on-call · service: checkout-api, orders-api
> At 12:00 the flash sale started. Traffic went from 120 to 650 requests per second. Checkout p99 is 10 s,
> 31 % of `POST /checkout` return 504. orders-api calls inventory (40 ms), billing (120 ms), email-svc
> (normally 900 ms, now 2.5 s) and analytics (200 ms) one after the other. Its HTTP pool is 256 connections.
12:04:17 ERR orders-api  TaskCanceledException: HttpClient.Timeout of 10 seconds elapsing
1. A before/after report with numbers that shows why it failed and what moving email and analytics behind an
2. The number of email workers needed so the backlog never exceeds the agreed limit and is empty after the sale.
3. Fraud wants to replay the sale from 12:00: a log that can reset a group to a point in time.

steps.title: Before and after
prompt: Write `List<string> Report(int rps, int poolSize, (string Name, int LatencyMs, bool NeededForReply)[] hops)`
returning three lines:
1. `"before: {latency} ms, {inFlight} in flight, pool {poolSize}: {verdict}"` where `latency` is the sum of
**all** hops, `inFlight` Little's law rounded up, and `verdict` is `"SATURATED"` when `inFlight > poolSize`,
else `"ok"`.
2. `"after: ..."`, the same format but counting **only** the hops needed for the reply.
3. `"events: OrderPlaced -> {names}"` with the names of the hops not needed for the reply, in order, joined
with `", "`, or `"events: none"` if every hop is needed.
```text
Report(650, 256, [inventory 40 needed, billing 120 needed, email 2500, analytics 200])
before: 2860 ms, 1859 in flight, pool 256: SATURATED
after: 160 ms, 104 in flight, pool 256: ok
events: OrderPlaced -> email, analytics
starter: List<string> Report(int rps, int poolSize, (string Name, int LatencyMs, bool NeededForReply)[] hops)
solution: List<string> Report(int rps, int poolSize, (string Name, int LatencyMs, bool NeededForReply)[] hops)
hints: Write a small local function that formats one line for a given latency.
The after-latency sums only the hops with `NeededForReply`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoSale = new (string, int, bool)[] { ("inventory", 40, true), ("billing", 120, true), ("email", 2500, false), ("analytics", 200, false) };

Dojo.Eq("the flash sale report", new List<string> { "before: 2860 ms, 1859 in flight, pool 256: SATURATED", "after: 160 ms, 104 in flight, pool 256: ok", "events: OrderPlaced -> email, analytics" }, Report(650, 256, dojoSale));

Dojo.Eq("a quiet day", new List<string> { "before: 2860 ms, 344 in flight, pool 400: ok", "after: 160 ms, 20 in flight, pool 400: ok", "events: OrderPlaced -> email, analytics" }, Report(120, 400, dojoSale));
var dojoNeeded = new (string, int, bool)[] { ("auth", 30, true), ("pricing", 70, true) };
Dojo.Eq("nothing to move", new List<string> { "before: 100 ms, 100 in flight, pool 50: SATURATED", "after: 100 ms, 100 in flight, pool 50: SATURATED", "events: none" }, Report(1000, 50, dojoNeeded));

steps.title: Size the email workers
prompt: The email queue receives `arrivalsPerSec[i]` messages in second `i`. Each worker sends `perWorkerPerSec`
emails per second. Every second, first the arrivals join the queue, then the workers take up to
`workers × perWorkerPerSec` messages.
Write `int WorkersNeeded(int[] arrivalsPerSec, int perWorkerPerSec, int maxBacklog)`: the **smallest number of
workers (at least 1)** such that the depth after every second is at most `maxBacklog` **and** the queue is
empty after the last second.
```text
8 workers (400/s): depth 250, 500, 750 → over the limit
starter: int WorkersNeeded(int[] arrivalsPerSec, int perWorkerPerSec, int maxBacklog)
solution: int WorkersNeeded(int[] arrivalsPerSec, int perWorkerPerSec, int maxBacklog)
hints: Try 1, 2, 3, ... workers and simulate each one; return the first that passes.
A run fails as soon as the depth goes over `maxBacklog`; it passes only if the final depth is 0.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("the flash sale needs 9 workers", 9, WorkersNeeded(new[] { 650, 650, 650, 100, 100, 100 }, 50, 600));
Dojo.Eq("no backlog allowed: keep up with the peak", 13, WorkersNeeded(new[] { 650, 650, 650, 100, 100, 100 }, 50, 0));
Dojo.Eq("the queue must be empty at the end", 3, WorkersNeeded(new[] { 300, 300 }, 100, 1000));
Dojo.Eq("no traffic still needs one worker", 1, WorkersNeeded(new[] { 0, 0 }, 50, 0));

steps.title: Replay the sale from 12:00
prompt: Fraud wants to replay from a point in time, like
`kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets --to-datetime 2026-11-20T12:00:00.000`.
Write a class `SaleLog`:
- `long Append(long timestampMs, string value)`: appends and returns the offset. Timestamps never decrease.
- `long EndOffset`.
- `void Join(string group, bool fromEarliest)`: as before (`0` or `EndOffset`); joining again changes nothing.
- `List<string> Poll(string group, int max)`: up to `max` values from the group's position, then advances it.
Unknown group → `InvalidOperationException`.
- `long Lag(string group)`: `EndOffset` minus the position.
- `long OffsetForTime(long timestampMs)`: the first offset whose timestamp is **at or after** `timestampMs`,
or `EndOffset` if there is none (this is what Kafka's `offsetsForTimes` answers).
- `void ResetToTime(string group, long timestampMs)`: moves the group to `OffsetForTime(timestampMs)`.
Unknown group → `InvalidOperationException`.
starter: public long Append(long timestampMs, string value) => 0;
public void Join(string group, bool fromEarliest) { }
public List<string> Poll(string group, int max) => new();
public void ResetToTime(string group, long timestampMs) { }
solution: readonly List<(long Ts, string Value)> records = new();
public long Append(long timestampMs, string value)
public void Join(string group, bool fromEarliest)
public List<string> Poll(string group, int max)
public long Lag(string group) => EndOffset - Position(group);
public void ResetToTime(string group, long timestampMs)
positions.TryGetValue(group, out var p) ? p : throw new InvalidOperationException($"group '{group}' has not joined");
hints: Store `(long Ts, string Value)` tuples; positions per group as before.
`OffsetForTime`: scan for the first record with `Ts >= timestampMs`, else `EndOffset`.
template: var dojoS = new SaleLog();
dojoS.Append(1000, "A1");
dojoS.Append(2000, "A2");
dojoS.Append(2000, "A3");
dojoS.Append(5000, "A4");
dojoS.Join("billing", fromEarliest: true);
Dojo.Eq("billing reads from the start", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A3" }, dojoS.Poll("billing", 3));
dojoS.Join("fraud", fromEarliest: false);
Dojo.Eq("fraud on latest has no lag", 0L, dojoS.Lag("fraud"));
Dojo.Eq("first offset at 12:00 (2000)", 1L, dojoS.OffsetForTime(2000));
Dojo.Eq("a time between records", 3L, dojoS.OffsetForTime(2500));
Dojo.Eq("a time after the end", 4L, dojoS.OffsetForTime(9000));
Dojo.Eq("a time before the start", 0L, dojoS.OffsetForTime(0));
dojoS.ResetToTime("fraud", 2000);
Dojo.Eq("fraud now has lag 3", 3L, dojoS.Lag("fraud"));
Dojo.Eq("fraud replays the sale", new List<string> { "A2", "A3", "A4" }, dojoS.Poll("fraud", 10));
Dojo.Eq("billing is not affected", new List<string> { "A4" }, dojoS.Poll("billing", 10));
Dojo.Eq("new records get the next offset", 4L, dojoS.Append(6000, "A5"));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("reset an unknown group", () => dojoS.ResetToTime("audit", 0));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("poll an unknown group", () => dojoS.Poll("audit", 1));
